text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE to #incidents — cross-region routing spike detected for route /v1/generate. Severity: P2. Trigger: 5xx rate from eu-west-1 -> 15% above baseline. Paging @jordan_net_oncall for network-oncall.

jordan_net_oncall: Ack, I'm on. Pulling up routing telemetry and policy eval logs. Any active customer tickets?

hannah_cs: multiple CS tickets coming in from EU customers — timeouts and long tail latency. Ticket #INC-7821 called in. One high-traffic tenant seeing many retries.

alex_sre: Seeing elevated 502/504s in eu-west-1 traces. Weirdly, a large fraction of traffic is being routed to us-east-1. Policy evals show a fallback path wrongly selected due to a priority mismatch.

maria_prod: @alex_sre can we pin /v1/generate to eu-west-1 (short-lived) to stop the blast while we investigate the policy change?

sam_engineer: prepping mitigation. Suspect recent rollout altered pin priority and a cached routing policy with low TTL propagated quickly.

alex_sre: Executing mitigation: override route pin for eu prefixes to eu-west-1. Command executed:
```
redwood route set --name /v1/generate --pin-region eu-west-1 --expires 3600
```

incident-bot: Action recorded by @alex_sre. Audit-id: au_9f3b. Current fallback chain snapshot: eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 -> us-west-2.

hannah_cs: Updating affected customer list and sending initial notification. ETA messaging: 30m. Leaving note for CS to escalate if SLA breach suspected.

dave_ops: Noted — there was a config tweak earlier that lowered DNS TTL from 300 -> 60s for faster rollouts. That would speed the spread of the bad policy. Recommend revert.

sam_engineer: Rolling back the TTL change on routing policy now:
```
redwood route config edit /v1/generate --set dns_ttl=300
```

alex_sre: After the pin and TTL rollback, error rate in EU dropped from ~12% -> ~2% within two minutes. Latency for EU-tenants trending back to baseline. Monitoring closely.

maria_prod: Are there any long-lived connections or LB caches that might keep directing traffic to the wrong region? Anything we need to flush?

jordan_net_oncall: Initiating routing-cache flush on proxies in eu-west-1 to clear stale policy entries:
```
kubectl exec -n routing-cache routing-proxy-0 -- /bin/sh -c 'redis-cli FLUSHDB'
```
Propagation started (~30s).

eng-lead: Good triage. Prepare a short handoff at 18:00 UTC to oncall-night. @jordan_net_oncall please include root cause hypothesis and mitigations taken.

jordan_net_oncall: Handoff summary: suspected root cause — policy rollout with incorrect priority + reduced dns_ttl amplified bad variant. Mitigations applied: 1) temporary region pin for /v1/generate, 2) reverted dns_ttl to 300s, 3) flushed routing caches. Audit: au_9f3b. Error rates stabilized. Passing to @sam_engineer for follow-up.

sam_engineer: Will open postmortem and PR to add rollout validation for pin priority and TTL sanity checks. Draft ETA 48h.

hannah_cs: Customers notified; no escalations to execs yet. One customer requested SLA credit — routing team to assess impact window against SLA.

maria_prod: Action items: sam = postmortem + gating rules; alex = add unit/integration tests for routing priority evaluation; jordan = update oncall runbook with cache flush steps and pin-override playbook.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to MITIGATED at 1719808120. Duration: ~39m. Participants logged: @jordan_net_oncall @alex_sre @sam_engineer @maria_prod @hannah_cs @dave_ops.

alex_sre: :thumbsup: Nice fast response everyone. I'll attach dashboard snapshots and a short metrics dump to the postmortem.

sam_engineer: (added) I'll include the faulty rollout diff and propose a canary policy that verifies region affinity under load before global promotion.

maria_prod: Thanks team — we'll reopen if anything regresses. Otherwise proceed with follow-ups and postmortem next steps.

(reacted :eyes: by eng-lead)
